requirement_text: NYU will continue to remain test-optional through the 2027-2028 application cycle. For students who elect to submit testing as part of their application, NYU has one of the most flexible testing policies of any college or university.
researcher_notes: Explicit, current, unambiguous test-optional statement. The immediately-relevant cycle for this research pass is entry Fall 2027 (cycle_year 2027); the page's own wording additionally confirms the policy is already committed through entry Fall 2028 ('2027-2028 application cycle'). Cross-checked against three independent NYU pages with no contradiction: this page; the All Freshmen Applicants page ('Standardized testing is optional for the upcoming application term', see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0002); and the Tisch Film & TV departmental page ('We are a ‘test optional’ program' / 'STANDARDIZED TEST SCORES ARE NOT REQUIRED TO APPLY TO THE FILM & TV DEPARTMENT', see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0026). Also specifically searched for an older/legacy pandemic-era test-optional or test-blind NYU page that might still be live and contradicting (the top failure mode flagged for this research wave) -- none was found; a March 2024 Washington Square News (NYU's independent student newspaper, not an official university source) article discussing NYU 'considering' reinstating testing was located but NOT used as evidence per this lane's official-sources-only rule -- it is noted here only to record that the possibility was checked, and the current official page clearly supersedes any such 2024 discussion by remaining test-optional through 2027-2028. NYU's public messaging is consistent across every official page fetched in this pass: this is a genuine 'clean, no conflict' finding, not an oversight.

requirement_text: If you choose to submit testing with your application, you can submit one of the following: SAT, ACT, Advanced Placement Exams, International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Program, GCE Advanced Level (A-Level), International Examinations. If you choose to submit standardized testing, you can only submit one form of testing. Applicants are welcome to self-report unofficial test scores for application review through their Applicant Portal.
researcher_notes: Combines a bulleted list of accepted test types with adjacent policy sentences from the same page; wording of each item preserved but list formatting and sentence order were adjusted, hence extracted_summary rather than verbatim_quoted. 'International Examinations' is NYU's own catch-all category name and is not further itemized on this page; see the International Qualifications Tool referenced on REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0021's source page for the country-specific detail NYU points applicants to.

requirement_text: Required if: English is not your first language (Your first language is the language that you learned first and speak best) AND During any of the 3 most recently completed academic years (prior to the current in-progress year): You have taken any coursework in a language other than English (excluding World Language courses), OR You have taken any English Language Support coursework (ESL, ELL, IB English B), OR You were enrolled in a bilingual curriculum.
researcher_notes: Trigger is defined by first-language and recent-schooling-language, not by citizenship/nationality -- a domestic (US-citizen) applicant whose first language is not English and who has taken ESL/ELL coursework recently would also be required to test. Recorded applies_to 'both' rather than 'international' for this reason.

requirement_text: Not required if: English is your first language (Your first language is the language that you learned first and speak best) OR All of your schooling for the three full consecutive academic years prior to the current year were taught entirely in English (excluding world language classes).
researcher_notes: MINOR PHRASING VARIANCE ACROSS TWO OFFICIAL PAGES (recorded rather than silently resolved, per this lane's discipline): this page anchors the 3-year English-medium exemption as 'the three full consecutive academic years prior to the current year,' while the All Freshmen Applicants page (source A, 'Step 2: Gather and Submit Necessary Documents' section) describes the same substantive exemption as 'at least 3 years of study where English is the sole language of instruction at the time of application submission.' Both point to the same 3-year English-medium-schooling threshold, but 'prior to the current year' and 'at the time of application submission' are not necessarily the same anchor point for a student applying mid-way through a school year. Not flagged as CONFLICTING_EVIDENCE (both describe one policy, not two contradictory policies) but worth a human check for edge-case applicants near the boundary.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT (Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test). We will accept results from the in-person version or the iBT Home Edition. Duolingo English Test. IELTS Academic (International English Language Testing System). PTE Academic (Pearson Test of English Academic). C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency (Cambridge English: Advanced or Proficiency). The above listed exams are the only English language tests we accept.
researcher_notes: Bulleted list reformatted into prose; no wording changed. NYU does NOT accept any other standardized test (SAT/ACT/AP/IB/A-Level/etc.) as a substitute for one of these five -- see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0014 for the explicit non-waiver statement.

requirement_text: We don’t have minimum score requirements, but competitive applicants will receive: 100 and above on the TOEFL iBT taken on or before January 20, 2026.
limitations: NOT A STATED MINIMUM: NYU explicitly disclaims a minimum score requirement in the same sentence ('We don’t have minimum score requirements'); this figure describes what 'competitive applicants' typically present, not a pass/fail eligibility cutoff. Should not be encoded as a hard threshold by a future structured_rule pass.
researcher_notes: Explicitly and unambiguously bounded to its own date range by the source itself ('taken on or before January 20, 2026') -- same pattern that scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md calls unambiguous for Edinburgh's pre-cutover TOEFL row. Companion row REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0007 covers the post-cutover (1-6 scale) side; together they show NYU handled the January 2026 ETS TOEFL rescale correctly (giving genuinely new-scale numbers post-cutover, including subscores) rather than exhibiting the stale-subtest-scale defect found at Glasgow and Boğaziçi elsewhere in this research effort.

requirement_text: 5 or above (overall score and subscores) on the TOEFL iBT taken on or after January 21, 2026.
limitations: NOT A STATED MINIMUM -- see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0006; 'competitive applicants will receive' framing, not a pass/fail cutoff.
researcher_notes: POSITIVE FINDING for the TOEFL-rescale trap this research wave was briefed to watch for: NYU gives genuinely new-scale (1-6) figures for both the overall score AND every subscore on the post-cutover side ('overall score and subscores'), rather than restating a stale 0-120-era subtest number after the cutover (the defect identified at Glasgow and Boğaziçi in this same research effort). Dated unambiguously to 'taken on or after January 21, 2026,' matching ETS's own effective date.

requirement_text: 135 and above on the Duolingo English Test
limitations: NOT A STATED MINIMUM -- see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0006. No Duolingo-specific test_scale enum value was supplied for this research pass (allowed list covers only TOEFL/IELTS/Cambridge/SAT scales), so the numeric threshold is recorded in requirement_text only and test_scale is left null rather than forcing an inexact enum match.

requirement_text: 7.5 and above on the IELTS Academic
limitations: NOT A STATED MINIMUM -- see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0006.
researcher_notes: IELTS 0-9 band scale is stable/unchanged (matches the cross-university audit finding in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md); no rescale ambiguity applies here.

requirement_text: 70 and above on the PTE Academic
limitations: NOT A STATED MINIMUM -- see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0006. No PTE-specific test_scale enum value was supplied for this research pass; threshold recorded in requirement_text only.

requirement_text: 191 and above on the Cambridge English Scale
limitations: NOT A STATED MINIMUM -- see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0006. Applies to C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency per REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0005's accepted-tests list.
researcher_notes: Cambridge English Scale is stable/unchanged (matches the cross-university audit finding in scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md).

requirement_text: We do not accept TOEFL iBT “My Best” scores or IELTS One Skill Retake. If you took the TOEFL iBT or IELTS, please send us your result from the test wherein you received the highest composite score.
limitations: NAMED EXCLUSION: excludes specific score provenances (TOEFL MyBest superscore, IELTS One Skill Retake) that could otherwise numerically satisfy REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0006/0007/0009. A bare threshold comparison cannot detect an excluded provenance; per scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md this requirement should evaluate to needs_manual_review rather than a silent pass/fail even when the submitted number clears the competitive benchmark.
researcher_notes: Near-identical in kind to Edinburgh's 'We do not accept IELTS One Skill Retake' / 'We do not accept TOEFL MyBest Score' exclusions and Koç's single-session-only rule found elsewhere in this research effort -- confirms this is a recurring cross-institutional trap, not an idiosyncratic one. The second sentence (submit the highest-composite SEPARATE sitting) is a different, permitted mechanic from MyBest superscoring (which recombines section scores across multiple sittings into one composite) -- MyBest is TOEFL's own official superscoring feature and is exactly what is excluded here.

requirement_text: applicants whose first language is not English are generally required to submit results from a proficiency exam taken within the last two years. Even if not strictly required, submitting these scores can provide valuable context to your application.
limitations: RECENCY CONSTRAINT: source states the exam must be taken 'within the last two years' but does not explicitly anchor the two-year window to a specific reference point (application submission date vs. enrollment/program start date) on this page. Per scalar-thresholds-are-not-enough.md's recency-rule finding, a stored score that was valid when taken can silently become stale without a max-age check; this requirement should evaluate to needs_manual_review rather than a silent pass, since the evaluator has no current concept of 'date test was taken' to compare against.
researcher_notes: Same shape as Edinburgh's Mathematics-qualification-age and English-qualification-age rules and Koç's 2-year test-validity rule found elsewhere in this research effort.

requirement_text: NYU does not waive the English language requirements based on the following exam results: SAT, ACT, AP, IGCSE, AS/A-Levels, International Baccalaureate Diploma (IBDP), including IB English A or B HL and SL, and other local national exams conducted in English.
researcher_notes: Genuinely useful negative finding: a naive assumption based on common patterns at peer institutions (where an English-medium AP/IB/A-Level record often waives the English-proficiency test) would get NYU wrong. NYU explicitly names IB English A/B (HL and SL) as NOT sufficient, despite IB English being taught and examined in English.

requirement_text: Am I Required to Interview with NYU? No. NYU does not offer interviews to any candidates.
researcher_notes: Clean negative confirmation, university-wide (this statement is on the English-testing FAQ page but is phrased generally, not scoped to international applicants only).

requirement_text: Contact information for one person (or, optionally, up to three maximum) who will complete a letter of recommendation. NYU requires one letter of recommendation from a teacher, counselor, coach, supervisor, or anyone else in a position of authority. If your recommender is unable to submit their letter through the Common Application, they can email it directly to admissions.docs@nyu.edu.
researcher_notes: One letter required; up to three accepted. Recommender need not be a teacher specifically -- 'counselor, coach, supervisor, or anyone else in a position of authority' is explicitly broader than the common 'academic teacher only' pattern at some peer schools.

requirement_text: Nonrefundable $85.00 application fee. Students who are unable to pay the application fee can request a fee waiver.
researcher_notes: Fee waiver available on request; mechanism/eligibility criteria for the waiver itself not detailed on this page. Note per REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0009's source page: NYU does NOT provide fee waivers for the separate English Language Proficiency exams even when a student qualifies for the application fee waiver.

requirement_text: A Self-reported Transcript and Academic Record System (STARS). All applicants will be invited to complete this after submitting their application.
researcher_notes: Self-reported academic record required of all applicants in addition to the school-submitted transcript/School Report; distinct from the (optional/if-available) Mid Year Report, see REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0019.

requirement_text: The Common Application Mid Year Report with updated academic record if mid-year grades are available. This should show your first semester senior year grades.
researcher_notes: Conditional on availability ('if mid-year grades are available'); most relevant to Regular Decision and Early Decision II applicants, since Early Decision I is decided (Dec 15) before first-semester senior grades typically post.

requirement_text: We find students are best prepared for NYU if they’ve studied the following subjects: English/Writing - 4 years; History/Social Studies - 3 to 4 years; Mathematics - 3 to 4 years; Laboratory Sciences - 3 to 4 years; Foreign Language - 3 to 4 years. Note: Our top applicants have taken demanding coursework in the above subjects for four years, however, we understand that not all students have options for choosing coursework depending on the type of school they are in. We will not hold students at a disadvantage if they do not meet these requirements if they did not have the option to do so.
researcher_notes: Explicitly recommended preparation, not a strict eligibility requirement -- NYU's own text disclaims penalizing students without access to this coursework. Should not be encoded as a hard prerequisite gate. See REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0021/0022/0023 for the school-specific (Stern/Tandon/Nursing) coursework guidance on the same source page.

requirement_text: If you are applying to the Stern School of Business or the Tandon School of Engineering, please note the following: International Baccalaureate: You are encouraged to take either the higher or standard level of Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Higher Level Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation. A-Levels: Students applying to the Stern School of Business or to Computer Science or Engineering majors are encouraged to take A-Level Mathematics. Applicants to the Stern School of Business should have Calculus or, at least, Precalculus on their transcript.
researcher_notes: Phrased as encouragement/preparation guidance ('should have ... on their transcript', 'encouraged to take'), not as a stated hard prerequisite with a rejection consequence. Stern undergraduates apply through the same Common Application / general NYU process (select Stern as primary program of interest); no separate Stern-specific supplemental essay or application system was found distinct from the general NYU first-year process during this research pass.

requirement_text: Applicants to the Tandon School of Engineering should have Physics, Chemistry, and Calculus (or at least Precalculus) on their transcript. A-Levels: Students applying to ... Computer Science or Engineering majors are encouraged to take A-Level Mathematics.
researcher_notes: Same source paragraph as REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0021 (Stern); the two schools are named together on NYU's 'Additional Program Requirements' section but the transcript guidance differs (Physics+Chemistry+Calculus for Tandon vs. Calculus/Precalculus alone for Stern), hence split into two program-scoped records. Phrased as guidance ('should have'), not a stated hard prerequisite.

requirement_text: Applications to the Meyers School of Nursing should have chemistry on their transcript.
researcher_notes: program_name recorded exactly as it appears in this source's text ('Meyers School of Nursing'); NYU's nursing school is more formally known elsewhere as the Rory Meyers College of Nursing -- flagging in case the canonical university_programs/school name on file differs and needs reconciliation at ingestion time. Only chemistry is mentioned for this school on this page; no further Nursing-specific detail was found during this research pass.

requirement_text: An audition or portfolio for specific artistic programs in the Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development and Tisch School of the Arts. For applicants to these programs, testing is optional and a required audition or portfolio can be submitted in place of standardized testing: ... Tisch requires an audition or portfolio for applicants to all programs.
researcher_notes: Tisch requires audition/portfolio for ALL of its undergraduate programs (Cinema Studies, Dance, Drama, Dramatic Writing, Film & Television, Game Design, IMA, Performance Studies, Photography & Imaging, Recorded Music per source K, tisch.nyu.edu/admissions/departmental-application-requirements), each with its own department-specific process (SlideRoom portfolio upload vs. live/recorded audition). This record captures the university-wide policy statement; department-level specifics were not individually researched for all 10 departments in this pass beyond the Film & TV illustration at REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0026. Standardized testing itself remains optional (not additionally required on top of the portfolio/audition) per REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0001/0026.

program_name: Steinhardt School of Culture, Education, and Human Development
requirement_text: Steinhardt requires an audition or portfolio for all applicants to the Music Department and a portfolio for those applying to Studio Art.
researcher_notes: Unlike Tisch (portfolio/audition required for ALL programs, REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0024), Steinhardt's requirement is scoped to only two specific programs within the school (Music Department; Studio Art) -- other Steinhardt programs are not stated to require a portfolio/audition on this page.

program_name: Tisch School of the Arts — Film & Television
requirement_text: Start your Common Application with the NYU supplement (choose Film & TV as your major). Start your Creative Portfolio via SlideRoom. (tischfilmandtv.slideroom.com) COMPLETE & SUBMIT BOTH by your chosen deadline. ... STANDARDIZED TEST SCORES ARE NOT REQUIRED TO APPLY TO THE FILM & TV DEPARTMENT. ... We DO NOT require the SAT/ACT or any other standardized test. We are a “test optional” program.
researcher_notes: Department-level illustration of REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0024's university-wide Tisch statement. This page explicitly states 'The 2026-2027 application is now open for first-year applicants,' which is the concrete year-anchor this research pass used to assign cycle_year 2027 (entry Fall 2027) to the dated deadline records in the companion deadlines file, since the university-wide Common Application deadline table on source A/B does not itself print a year.

requirement_text: If you apply for and are admitted through the early decision admission process, you are expected to enroll at NYU. In addition, you are expected to withdraw applications from other schools, and not submit any new applications after receiving an offer of admission. While we expect early decision applicants to honor their early decision commitment, we recognize that there may be extenuating circumstances. Exceptions are granted when an applicant is not admitted to their first choice NYU school, program, or campus, or when a students’ awarded financial aid package does not meet enough of the financial need for that student to be able to afford to attend. Any students who require greater flexibility or an exception should contact the admissions office to discuss their options and/or to be released from their early decision commitment.
researcher_notes: SCOPE: Early Decision I round specifically (see companion record REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0028 for Early Decision II). NYU's Early Decision FAQ page states this binding commitment ONCE, generically, covering 'the early decision admission process' without separately differentiating ED I from ED II terms -- unlike the task brief's hypothesis that NYU's page 'may state slightly different terms for each,' the terms found here are identical/undifferentiated between the two rounds; two records were still created per the research brief's instruction to treat ED I and ED II as separate companion records. Two named release valves are stated: (1) not admitted to first-choice NYU school/program/campus, (2) awarded financial aid package insufficient to meet demonstrated need. This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact -- should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review.

requirement_text: If you apply for and are admitted through the early decision admission process, you are expected to enroll at NYU. In addition, you are expected to withdraw applications from other schools, and not submit any new applications after receiving an offer of admission. While we expect early decision applicants to honor their early decision commitment, we recognize that there may be extenuating circumstances. Exceptions are granted when an applicant is not admitted to their first choice NYU school, program, or campus, or when a students’ awarded financial aid package does not meet enough of the financial need for that student to be able to afford to attend. Any students who require greater flexibility or an exception should contact the admissions office to discuss their options and/or to be released from their early decision commitment.
researcher_notes: SCOPE: Early Decision II round specifically (companion to REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0027, Early Decision I). Confirmed independently that NYU genuinely offers a second, later binding round: the Early Decision page's own deadline table lists both 'Early Decision I -- November 1 -- December 15' and 'Early Decision II -- January 1 -- February 15' explicitly, and the Decision Information (counselor) page and Tisch Film & TV departmental page both independently corroborate an 'Early Decision II' round with a January 1 deadline. This is a genuine, verified ED II round -- do not assume it mirrors Columbia, which wave 1 research found does NOT have an ED II. NYU's page does not state different binding terms for ED II vs ED I (both governed by the single FAQ quoted here). This is a binding contractual commitment, not a checkable eligibility fact -- should not be auto-converted into a structured_rule threshold by a future interpretation pass; needs human review.

requirement_text: Can I apply for regular decision if I don’t get in with early decision? Unfortunately, you cannot.
researcher_notes: IMPORTANT DISAMBIGUATION: this answers the case where an ED applicant is DENIED outright. It is a distinct outcome from DEFERRAL -- the Decision Information (counselor) page (source E) lists five possible December 15 ED outcomes: '1. Offer of Admission, 2. Offer of Admission to an Alternate Program of Interest, 3. Deferral, 4. Waitlist, 5. Denial.' A deferred ED applicant is automatically carried into the Early Decision II / Regular Decision pool for reconsideration without submitting a new application; that is NOT the scenario this FAQ answer forecloses. Only an applicant DENIED under Early Decision is barred from a subsequent Regular Decision application in the same cycle. This is a materially different mechanic from Columbia's (wave 1 finding: Columbia automatically defers non-admitted ED applicants into its RD pool and does not treat that as 'reapplying') and should not be assumed to generalize across institutions.

requirement_text: NYU’s New York campus is home to students from over 130 countries. All applicants, regardless of citizenship, are held to the same admissions standards and follow the same general process.
researcher_notes: General policy statement that admissions standards/process are citizenship-blind. Contrast with REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0033, which documents that NYU could NOT be confirmed (on any official page found in this pass) to make an equivalent explicit 'need-blind' or 'need-aware' statement specifically about how financial-aid applications factor into the ADMISSION decision itself for international applicants -- this statement is about admissions STANDARDS/PROCESS, not about whether requesting aid affects the outcome.

requirement_text: If you’re applying to NYU Abu Dhabi or NYU Shanghai, refer to their specific guidelines: All applicants to NYU Abu Dhabi. Chinese citizens applying to NYU Shanghai. All other applicants to NYU Shanghai.
researcher_notes: SCOPE BOUNDARY, recorded explicitly per task brief instruction: NYU Abu Dhabi and NYU Shanghai are real, distinct global campuses with their own separate admissions guideline pages (e.g. NYU Abu Dhabi's own 'Entry Requirements' page at nyuad.nyu.edu/en/apply/undergraduate/apply/entry-requirements.html) and, per the Shanghai case, citizenship-conditional guidance ('Chinese citizens' vs 'all other applicants' are pointed to different Shanghai guideline pages). All three campuses share ONE submission platform -- the Common Application, where an applicant selects a primary campus/program of interest with up to two alternates (per source A: 'You'll be able to choose your campus(es) and program(s) of interest on the NYU-specific page of the Common Application') -- but shared submission mechanics do not imply identical entry requirements. This research pass is scoped to the New York campus's undergraduate admissions only, per task brief; NYU Abu Dhabi and NYU Shanghai specific requirements/deadlines were deliberately NOT researched or recorded in this file and would need their own dedicated research pass.

requirement_text: Need-based scholarships are available to non-U.S. citizens or permanent residents applying as first-year students. Submit the CSS Profile by the deadline for consideration. Transfer students and those pursuing a second bachelor’s degree are not eligible for NYU institutional aid.
researcher_notes: Extracted from the 'Financing Your Education' accordion panel on the International Applicants page, which is CSS-hidden by default (aria-hidden/accordion collapsed) but present in the page DOM -- confirmed present via direct DOM inspection since the standard rendered-text extraction does not expand collapsed accordions. See REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0033 for the broader, dated NYU Promise commitment this pairs with, and REQ-2026-08-21-NYU0034 for the post-admission certification-of-finances requirement mentioned on the same panel.

requirement_text: All students admitted as first-year undergraduate students to our New York campus and who apply for financial aid by the financial aid deadlines will have 100% of their demonstrated need met, regardless of citizenship status. That includes international applicants, as well as undocumented students.
researcher_notes: CONTRAST WITH WAVE 1 FINDING, as flagged by the task brief: this is a MORE generous, not less generous, aid commitment than initially hypothesized for NYU relative to the Ivies in wave 1. Per the same source page: 'Beginning in the 2024-25 academic year, President Linda G. Mills expanded NYU's commitment to affordability through The NYU Promise, guaranteeing that every undergraduate–domestic and international–who start as a first-year student admitted to our New York campus will have 100% of their demonstrated need met through a combination of scholarships and grants. In addition, families with income less than $100,000 and who hold typical assets will not have to pay tuition.' This is a POST-ADMISSION aid guarantee (it describes what happens once a student is admitted and applies for aid by the deadline), not an explicit statement about whether financial need is considered DURING the admission decision itself for international applicants. IMPORTANT GAP, reported per task brief's specific request: despite searching the Standardized Tests page, the Financial Aid FAQ page (including the expanded 'What types of financial aid are available to international students attending NYU?' accordion answer), this NYU Promise page, and the International Applicants page's 'Financing Your Education' accordion, NO official nyu.edu page fetched in this research pass was found to use explicit 'need-blind' or 'need-aware' language describing NYU's ADMISSION decision process for international applicants. Secondary/consulting sources (e.g. CollegeVine, and unverified Quora answers surfaced by search) claim NYU is 'need-blind for domestic students, need-aware for international students,' with one such secondary source additionally claiming a 'small number' of applicants have been affected by ability-to-pay considerations 'beginning in Fall 2021' -- per this lane's evidence discipline (official sources only, no aggregators/consulting sites, no AI prior knowledge), that specific admissions-need-aware claim is NOT recorded as a verified requirement in this dataset and should be treated as unconfirmed rather than true or false. This is an explicit, deliberate 'unknown' -- not an oversight -- and should be a priority for a future official-source check (e.g. NYU's Common Data Set, if publicly posted) rather than being filled in from secondary sources.

requirement_text: Admitted students must submit a certification of finances showing proof of funding for four years of study. ... Fill out the NYU Application for Certificate of Eligibility (AFCOE) online after you’re admitted to the university and pay your enrollment deposit. Submit supporting documents, as well. This must be done before you’re issued a student visa (Form I-20) or exchange visitor visa (Form DS-2019).
researcher_notes: Post-admission, pre-enrollment requirement (not an admission-decision eligibility criterion); required for visa issuance (F-1 Form I-20 / J-1 Form DS-2019). Same source panel also states F-1/J-1 visa holders 'are generally not allowed to work in the U.S. to help pay for their education and are required to pursue a full-time course load each semester.'
